comment: T4 baseline (docs/TESTING.md). `nodes` counts every node and `retainedNodes` only those carrying a mesh of their own (the Labels). Since P1 all of them draw: `buffersAlive` is 2 whatever the node count - the growing vertex buffer and the fullscreen quad the filter passes draw - because no node owns one any more. It read 3 until the P1 review, and that 3 was a C function returning the literal 3: gated against the literal, so the assertion compared a constant to a constant and would have kept passing if every Label allocated a buffer again. It also miscounted, since the third thing it named was the font image and not a buffer. It is made-minus-freed at the sg_make_buffer/sg_destroy_buffer sites now, and was checked by allocating one extra buffer and watching it read 3, then 2 again, and `vertices` is what proves every label emitted geometry instead of being dropped by a full pool. `ui.draws` is 20000 and not 253 because the bench alternates a white-texture card with a font-texture label on every node; the unified pipeline and the white texel in the glyph atlas that collapse that are P2's. Counters gate hard; milliseconds only report, with a warn threshold, because this is a shared developer box. How much that matters, measured 2026-09-20 after the sampler commit: the same `benchSprites` binary that read 1.63 ms when this file was written reads 1.87-2.09 ms on a box sitting at 54% CPU from other work, which is 1.28x and most of the way to the 1.5x warn. The numbers below were not re-taken to make that go away, and the warn factor was not raised: a threshold moved to fit the reading stops being a threshold. What a millisecond row can answer is *relative* regression, and only one way - build both commits, run them interleaved on the same box in the same minute. Done for the sampler commit against its parent `06c2bd0`: PREV 1.96/2.09/1.87/2.00 against NOW 1.98/1.97/1.92/1.96, mean 1.98 vs 1.96, so guardrail 8 holds and the gap to 1.63 is the machine. A gate WARN on a millisecond row means re-run that A/B, not that the phase regressed — SCENE-SCALE.md:197 records its own numbers being taken at load average 14-17. buffersAlive 2 -> 3 on 2026-09-21, at P2's sprite pipeline: the third is the unit quad the instanced sprite path steps per vertex, a 48-byte static buffer made once at setup beside the growing vertex buffer and the filter passes' fullscreen quad. The gate caught this rather than a reader noticing - which is the point of the counter having been moved off a literal at P1, and it is the second time in one session it has earned that. What would make 3 wrong is growth with the node count: three is three at 10 000 nodes and at 20 000, and a number that scales is the defect this counter exists to catch. THE INSTANCED SPRITE PATH, 2026-09-21. Every moved row below is arithmetic, and each one is written out because a number that changed without an explanation is the defect this file keeps finding. sprites.vertices 60000 -> 0: every sprite is an instance now, so the vertex stream is empty. sprites.uploadBytes 1920000 -> 640000, exactly 10000 x 64 B, a 3x cut that is the 192 B quad becoming a 64 B instance. ui.vertices 293340 -> 233340, exactly 60000 fewer, which is the 10000 cards x 6 vertices that became instances; the labels are still vertices because the glyph mode is P2's next piece. ui.uploadBytes 9386880 -> 8106880, down 1280000 = 10000 x (192 - 64). ui.uploads 1 -> 2 because the vertex stream and the instance stream are two appends into one buffer; concatenating them would mean copying the whole vertex stream through a staging buffer to save a call that costs nothing, so the counter is allowed to say 2 rather than the code pretending it is 1. ui.draws is UNCHANGED at 20000: P2's headline number is the unified UI pipeline's, not this commit's, and a sprite path that moved it would be measuring something else. MILLISECONDS: sprites.present 2.5 -> 1.8, and that is a claim, so it was proven the only way this file accepts - an interleaved same-box A/B against 74ad3f8 on a box checked quiet first (9-13% CPU), six alternating pairs, NOW lower in all six: PREV 2.58/2.36/2.45/2.35/2.27/2.39 mean 2.40 against NOW 2.03/1.89/1.71/1.74/1.61/1.99 mean 1.83, a 24% improvement. ui.present is not re-baselined here: it moved by less than its own spread and a single reading is not evidence. Keys are nested rather than dotted so tests/bench/check.ms can read them through the JsonValue accessors. MILLISECONDS RE-TAKEN 2026-09-21 (F-14, at P2's first step). The rows above used to read ui 17.8 and sprites 1.63, and neither could be reproduced by the very commit they came from. Measured on a QUIET box - 10.8% CPU mean over five one-second samples, checked before the runs and not after the fact - by an interleaved same-box A/B between 6a997ee (P1's land, rebuilt from a git archive) and 544ea4a, six alternating pairs of each bench: ui P1 19.95 (19.69-20.30) against NOW 19.86 (19.34-20.16); sprites P1 2.51 (2.24-3.06) against NOW 2.48 (2.27-2.82). A standalone eight-run series of the current binaries alone, which perturbs less, reads ui 20.33 (20.19-21.08) and sprites 2.76 (2.52-2.86). TWO CONCLUSIONS, both measured. (1) GUARDRAIL 8 HOLDS: nothing between P1's land and here - the commit hook, the rebase onto void3d's M6 - moved either row; the two columns of the A/B are inside each other's spread. (2) The old numbers were WRONG, not stale-because-busy. This file used to explain the gap to 1.63 as the machine, citing a run at 54% CPU. That explanation does not survive: at 10.8% CPU, P1's OWN binary reads 2.51. THIS IS NOT A THRESHOLD MOVED TO FIT A READING, which this file forbids and still forbids. warnFactor is unchanged at 1.5. What changed is the baseline a threshold is taken from, because the old baseline was shown unreproducible by the binary of the commit that produced it, on a box proven quiet, in an A/B rather than in a single run. The practical consequence of leaving it was a gate that printed WARN sprites.present.ms on every green run - a warning that always fires is a warning nobody reads. BOX MODE, 2026-09-21. A Rect is now a UI instance in box mode rather than a sprite instance, so its edge coverage is computed analytically instead of coming from the rasteriser. Arithmetic for every moved row. ui.uploadBytes 8106880 -> 8546880, exactly +440000 = 10000 cards x (108 - 64): the card's instance grew from the sprite stride to the UI stride, and that is the price of the mode lane. ui.vertices UNCHANGED at 233340 - the labels are still vertices, the glyph mode is the next piece. ui.draws UNCHANGED at 20000, and this is the one to read carefully: the scene still alternates card and label on every node, and they still differ in BOTH view and pipeline, so closing one of the two moves nothing. A reader who expects the headline to move here will conclude the phase failed; it has not started moving yet. ui.uploads still 2: the vertex stream and the UI instance stream, two appends into one buffer. TWO NEW GATED COUNTERS, A2: uiInstances and spriteInstances, per scene. The shape A2 asks for is draws falling WHILE instances hold at the node count - instances falling with draws means nodes were dropped, and draws alone cannot tell those apart. Both streams are gated per scene rather than one number, which makes B5 a gated fact: sprites.uiInstances is 0, so a sprite-only frame provably emits nothing into the UI pipeline. A per-mode count could not say that, because an empty frame reads zero of every mode too. A4's control for the new pair was run: ui.uiInstances read 0 before the emitter was switched and 10000 after, and it becomes 20000 when the labels join in glyph mode. sprites.spriteInstances is unchanged at 10000, which is guardrail 8 stated as a number.

taken.renderer: the display list: one growing vertex buffer, one upload, no per-node sg_buffer
